title.en: Show that a simple pendulum performs SHM for small angles

say.en: Galileo timed a swinging lamp in a cathedral with his pulse. Big swings or small, each took the same time. Why? In this lesson: Show that a simple pendulum performs SHM for small angles.
Use T equals 2 pi the square root of (L over g).
Find g with a pendulum.

title.en: Why a pendulum is simple harmonic

body.en: A bob of mass m on a light string of length L, displaced by angle θ, feels a restoring torque τ = −mgL sin θ. For small angles sin θ ≈ θ (in radians), so τ ≈ −mgLθ: the angular acceleration is proportional to θ and opposite to it, which is SHM with ω = √(g/L).
body.kn: θ ಕೋನದಷ್ಟು ಸರಿಸಿದ ಲೋಲಕದ ಮೇಲೆ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಟಾರ್ಕ್ τ = −mgL sin θ. ಸಣ್ಣ ಕೋನಕ್ಕೆ sin θ ≈ θ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು ω = √(g/L) ಇರುವ ಸ.ಸಂ.ಚ.

title.en: Why the pendulum is simple harmonic

say.en: A bob of mass m hangs on a string of length L. Pull it aside through a small angle theta.
Its weight m g acts down. The part m g sin theta acts along the arc, back towards the mean position. The tension cancels the rest.
The restoring torque is minus m g L sin theta. For small angles sin theta is about theta, so the torque is proportional to theta: SHM.
The period is 2 pi root L over g. It does not depend on the mass, or on the amplitude if it is small.
A seconds pendulum has T = 2 seconds: its length is g over pi squared, about 0.993 metres. On the Moon, a 1.5 metre pendulum takes about 6.0 seconds.
T grows as the square root of L, so T squared against L is a straight line. Its slope, 4 pi squared over g, gives g.

body.en: The *period* is T = 2π√(L/g). It does not depend on the mass of the bob, nor on the amplitude as long as it is small. A seconds pendulum has a period of 2 s; its length is about 0.99 m on Earth. Measuring T for a known L gives g = 4π²L/T².
body.kn: ಆವರ್ತಕಾಲ T = 2π√(L/g). ಇದು ಗುಂಡಿನ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಣ್ಣ ಕಂಪನ ವಿಸ್ತಾರವನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಸೆಕೆಂಡ್ ಲೋಲಕದ ಆವರ್ತಕಾಲ 2 s, ಉದ್ದ ಸುಮಾರು 0.99 m.

L equals gT squared/4 pi squared.
L equals 9.8 times 4 divided by 39.48.
L is approximately 0.993 metres.
